items.title: What Stablecoins and LLMs Have in Common — Amira Valliani from the Solana Foundation
items.summary: Amira Valliani on what AI and crypto have in common: "You see tokens in blockchain worlds, and now you see tokens in AI worlds. And it's tokens all the way down. So if you think about what is a token, it's a machine-readable format of an asset. And you're just seeing an enormous growth of tokens across the board. And you see tokens as part of tokenizers and LLMs, but you also see tokens in terms of growth of real world assets, stable coins all across the board. This growth has started. It's just going to be massive over the next 10 years, and it's going to be really obvious that anything that's an asset can be machine-readable as a token." — Amira Valliani, Head of Payments Growth at Solana Foundation, with @jd_durkin on @FINTECHTVglobal at @Money2020Tv

items.title: "This is not a pilot" – Solana's Nick Ducoff on the DTCC's Integration with Solana
items.summary: ​@TheDTCC processed over $4 quadrillion in transactions last year. Now it's connecting to @solana: "The DTCC tokenization service will connect to Solana's public network. DTS, as they call it, launched recently this past month, October 28th, and the Solana integration is planned for the second half of 2027. It's expected to support the fast conversion of eligible traditional assets into tokenized form, plus full tokenization lifecycle functionality. And it's incredibly important because, as you know, DTCC is the premier post-trade infrastructure for global finance. Over $4 quadrillion in transactions were processed last year by the DTCC. And when it connects to a tokenization service, to a network like Solana, it signals to the entire industry that tokenized securities are becoming real market infrastructure, and this is not a pilot." — Nick Ducoff, GM of Institutional at Solana Foundation on @theblockcrypto with Gareth Jenkinson
